key_insight: AI-derived deviations from personalised healthy cardiac “digital twins” captured heart-shape and motion patterns associated with outcome risk beyond conventional cardiac measurements.
clinical_relevance: These research scores may improve risk stratification despite preserved ejection fraction, but their value for guiding clinical care remains unproven.
method: Model expected healthy cardiac function using age, sex, and body habitus.
Measure individual deviations using statistical shape and deep generative cardiac representations.
Test added risk-prediction value beyond ejection fraction, volumes, myocardial mass, and strain.
evidence_signal: Two UK Biobank cohorts (n=52,365 and up to 39,376) showed representation-specific gains in preserved-EF participants: atrial fibrillation ΔC=+0.068 (+0.063 cross-validated) for HeartSSM and stroke ΔC=+0.024 for MeshHeart cVAE, with Gaussian-noise placebo checks.
watch_item: Outcome signals differed by representation; the external cohort of 315 healthy volunteers assessed transfer across imaging settings, not external outcome prediction.
paper_title: Personalised normative cardiac phenotyping reveals clinically relevant heterogeneity in cardiac shape and outcome risk
